subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files as part of the core bootstrap-extra-files hook contract?
rationale: The requested behavior changes which workspace content enters deterministic startup context and expands user-facing hook configuration semantics, so automation cannot choose the product/security boundary on its own.

options.title: Approve explicit in-workspace files
options.body: Allow custom basenames only when explicitly configured and still protected by workspace containment, size budgets, session filtering, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary file injection and keep operators on first-class workspace filenames or manual reads until a broader context API exists.

options.title: Defer to a broader context API
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers design a larger context-loading contract covering discovery, trust, session scoping, and diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit in-workspace files
recommendation.body: Allow custom basenames only when explicitly configured and still protected by workspace containment, size budgets, session filtering, docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has direct history in the boundary-safe bootstrap read path and prior review routing identified him as the likely product-boundary decision owner.
